findings.text: Two active decisions are implemented correctly but have no test, so a later refactor could break them silently. Decision isHeld-name-and-unreadable says reservedBy of empty string counts as set; `if (!book?.reservedBy) return false` passes every store test. Decision at-uncomparable-warns says the warning fires whatever the book, so a caller bug shows even on a free book; moving the warning after the free-book return also passes every store test, because the warning test only uses a held book. The current code does both correctly (probe: empty-string reservedBy is held; a free book with a bad at warns once). Adding one assertion for each would close this.

findings.text: If writing the pid fails just after the lock is created (for example on a full disk), acquireLock rejects without removing the lock or closing its handle. The caller gets a loud raw error, but the empty lock stays behind and other writers report busy until the 30-second age rule clears it. It recovers by itself and only happens when the disk is already failing, so this does not breach A4. Closing and unlinking in a catch around that write would tidy it.

reasons: Prior directive 1 and R-8 are resolved: isHeld warns once per call on an uncomparable at (invalid Date, garbage text, null, true, {}, NaN, Infinity), keeps a dated book held, and names nobody. null no longer coerces to the epoch.

R-9 is resolved by the strict ISO check under decision strict-iso-instants: '8 November' stays held and warns as unreadable. Mutant lax fails 3 tests.
A1 met: updateShelf loads under the lock, applies change, and saves only if change did not refuse. The T-27 witness fails against an in-place writer.
A2 met: the temp name is unique per write and in the same directory. A failed write mid-file or at rename leaves the old file whole with no stray (EFBIG experiment and EISDIR test).
A3 met: child-process hammer and twenty in-process tests pass. My own stress of 8 processes x 30 and 16 processes x 10, 3 rounds each, lost nothing, had no failures and left no files.
A4 met: dead-pid and aged locks are broken; a live lock gives ShelfBusyError with code SHELF_BUSY after 5s.
A5 met: isHeld is exported with the decided readings; on the seed data b2 is held and warns once per load, by id.
A6 met: docs/systems/store.md records the protocol, the reason for the lock and the accepted residual races.
Non-goals respected: no routes, pages, commands, dependencies or migration; only store, tests and the system note changed.
